title: Improve configuring temporary file location
description:
Shortcomings of #316 wrt the present issue: `CALLR_TMPDIR` is configurable, yes, but configuration needs to happen before loading `callr`, and cannot be changed after loading `callr` without breaking things. This prevents using a different directory for each call (the `callr` subprocess needs to have write access).

Cf. https://github.com/r-lib/callr/issues/262#issuecomment-5784512226

title: Allow to configure location of boilerplate and input/output files
description:
As a follow-up question to #261, I'd like to be able to use [`bubblewrap`](https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap) to isolate the different `callr` subprocesses coming from the same parent process. Currently it seems all `callr::r` calls will reference the same `.so` files and read inputs and write outputs to the same temporary folder.

Would it be possible to store the reused files in a separate folder (so that that one can be mounted read-only), and the input/output files in another folder so that that one can be mounted read-write separately?

Additionally would it be possible to have an easy way to know and/or configure where those are located?

There are probably cross-platform concerns there too maybe, although I am not sure whether many folders vs one is so big of a deal.

title: WISH: r_process$cleanup(close_connections = TRUE)
description:
If one launches too many callr processes while keeping track of them all, one can run out of file descriptors, although the processes have completed. This results in errors on "Too many open files".

# Example

```r

max_fd <- as.integer(system2("ulimit", args = "-n", stdout = TRUE))
cat("Max number of open files:", max_fd, "\n")

n <- ceiling(max_fd / 3)
processes <- list()
for (ii in 1:n) {
  cat(sprintf("\r%04d/%04d", ii, n))
  process <- callr::r_bg(function() NULL, stdout = "|", stderr = "|")
  process$wait()
  void <- process$read_all_output()
  void <- process$read_all_error()
  process$cleanup()
  processes[[ii]] <- process  ## prevent garbage collector from cleaning up
}
cat("\n")
```

Results in

title: Signal interrupts are not propagated to worker nodes in background sessions with `parallel` clusters
description:
Suppose you have the following background `session` object with a `parallel` `cluster` object.

```r
# Create a new `R` background session.
session <- callr::r_session$new()

# Create a cluster with two worker processes and record the process IDs.
worker_pids <- session$run(function() {
    # Create a cluster.
    cluster <<- parallel::makeCluster(spec = 2, type = "PSOCK")

    # Return the worker process IDs.
    return(unlist(parallel::clusterCall(cluster, Sys.getpid)))
})

# Run a task in the background that keeps the cluster busy indefinitely.
session$call(function() {
    # Send the task to the cluster workers.
    parallel::parSapply(cluster, 1:10, function(x) {
        # An infinite loop.
        while (TRUE) { Sys.sleep(0.0001) }
    })
})

# Interrupt the session.
session$interrupt()

# Read the session interruption condition.
session$read()

# Confirm the session is `idle`.
session$get_state()
```

The following will hang indefinitely on `macOS` because the workers are still busy (i.e., I believe the `SIGINT` signal is not propagated to the workers). However, it will output as expected on `Windows`.

```r
# Send the run and output the results.
session$run(function() {
    parallel::clusterCall(cluster, print, "Subsequent cluster call.")
})
```

At this point I sent a manual interrupt (i.e., `Ctrl + C`) on `macOS`.

```r
# Close the session.
session$close()

# Remove the reference to the `session` object.
rm(session)

# Request garbage collection.
gc(full = TRUE)
```

On `macOS` the worker processes are still running.

```r
# Check the status of the worker processes.
lapply(worker_pids, function(pid) {
    ps::ps_is_running(
        ps::ps_handle(pid)
    )
})

# Clean.
tools::pskill(worker_pids, tools::SIGTERM)
```

Is this expected behavior? Am I missing something obvious?

title: rscript(timeout = ...) hangs when child errors and stderr = "2>&1" on Windows
description:
## Summary

On Windows, `callr::rscript()` hangs indefinitely when:

- the child script terminates with `stop()` (non-zero exit), and
- `stderr = "2>&1"`, and
- `fail_on_status = FALSE`,

even with an explicit `timeout = ...`. The timeout never fires; the call never returns. Repeating the same call with `stderr = "|"` (separate capture) has not yet been tested but is the next thing to try.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 10 (build 19045) |
| R | 4.6.0 (2026-04-24 ucrt), x86_64-w64-mingw32 |
| Rtools | Rtools45 |
| callr | 3.7.6 |

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, R 4.6.0, callr 3.7.6) does **not** hang on the same call — the timeout fires correctly and the merged stdout+stderr comes back with the `Error: test error` text.

## Reproduction

```r
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
writeLines("stop('test error')", tmp)

# Hangs forever on Windows. timeout = 10 does NOT fire.
res <- callr::rscript(tmp,
                      show = FALSE,
                      fail_on_status = FALSE,
                      timeout = 10,
                      stdout = "|",
                      stderr = "2>&1")
```

On Windows, the call prints nothing and never returns. R has to be killed externally (`Stop-Process -Force`). On Linux the same call returns in well under a second with a populated `res$stdout` containing the error text.

## Expected

Either:
- the call returns normally with `res$stdout` containing the merged error output (the Linux behavior), or
- the `timeout = 10` fires and `res$timeout` is `TRUE`.

## Actual

The call blocks indefinitely. The 10s timeout is ignored. Externally killing the parent R process is the only way out.

## Context

Found while running `R CMD check --as-cran` on a package that wraps `callr::rscript()` as a "fresh-subprocess R evaluator" tool — the test case that triggers it is one line of subprocess code (`stop('test error')`) and it deadlocked the whole check. Local workaround on our side is to gate the failing test under `tinytest::at_home()`, but the underlying behavior of `rscript(timeout = ...)` not bounding the call on Windows is the real bug.

I haven't yet narrowed which flag in the trio (`stderr = "2>&1"`, `fail_on_status = FALSE`, the `stop()` itself) is the load-bearing one — happy to run more reductions if useful.

title: r_bg exit status always 0
description:
`callr::r_bg` always returns 0 even on error, despite R's default behavior (from `?q`: _The default error handler for non-interactive use effectively calls `q("no", 1, FALSE)` and returns error status 1_.)

```bash
$ echo 'quux' | R --vanilla --quiet
> quux
Error: object 'quux' not found
Execution halted
$ echo $?
1
```

With `callr` though, we always get 0:

```r
proc <- callr::r_bg(function() quux)
proc$read_all_output()
# [1] "WARNING: ignoring environment value of R_HOME\n"
proc$read_all_error()
# [1] "Error in (function ()  : object 'quux' not found\n"
proc$get_exit_status()
# [1] 0
```

I recognize I can use `rscript_process` to get the desired effect:

```r
writeLines("quux", "quux.R")
proc <- callr::rscript_process$new(callr::rscript_process_options(script="quux.R"))
proc$read_all_output()
# [1] "WARNING: ignoring environment value of R_HOME\n"
proc$read_all_error()
# [1] "Error: object 'quux' not found\nExecution halted\n"
proc$get_exit_status()
# [1] 1
```

I suggest would be more consistent if the `error=` and `interrupt=` handlers in the wrapper used by `callr::r_bg` end with `q(save="no", status=1)`.

```diff
modified   R/script.R
@@ -36,6 +36,7 @@ make_vanilla_script_expr <- function(expr_file, res, error,
       }
 
       base::saveRDS(base::list("error", e2, e), file = base::paste0(`__res__`, ".error"))
+      q(save = "no", status = 1)
     }, list(
          `__res__` = res,
          `__traceback__` = getOption("callr.traceback", FALSE)
```

With that, I see the desired behavior:

```r
devtools::load_all()
proc <- callr::r_bg(function() quux)
proc$read_all_output()
# [1] "WARNING: ignoring environment value of R_HOME\n"
proc$read_all_error()
# [1] ""
proc$get_exit_status()
# [1] 1
```

Are there other aspects that would need to be addressed as well? (That is, what else could be changed for this to be a more complete solution?) Or is there rationale for having `r_bg` always return status 0?

I'm running R-4.3.3 and callr_3.7.6 within emacs/ess on ubuntu-24.04.

title: warnings are suppressed in r_session$call()
description:
It would be nice if the status code marked that a warning had occurred. At the moment, one can at best get the warning message from `stdout`, but `code` is still 200, so there's no way of differentiating a valid output from a warning. 

For example:
```R
rs <- callr::r_session$new()
rs$call(function() warning("warning message"))
rs$read()

# $code
# [1] 200
# 
# $message
# [1] "done callr-rs-result-2b3a9589b28e4"
# 
# $result
# [1] "warning message"
# 
# $stdout
# [1] ""
# 
# $stderr
# [1] ""
# 
# $error
# NULL
# 
# attr(,"class")
# [1] "callr_session_result"
```

Using a different error code or adding a `warning` field to the results would allow to retrieve whether a warning had occurred.

The only workaround I've found is to turn the warnings into options within the session with `rs$run(function() options(warn = 2))`, and then parse the `error` field to see if it contains the string "(converted from warning)". This is quite clumsy, it's effective only in an English locale, and with this it's impossible to keep track of cases when both warnings and errors occur.

In any case, the handling of warnings by `callr` should be documented.

title: Preserve the color theme of the parent process?
description:
## Issue

From https://github.com/r-lib/cli/issues/467, `cli` colors printed from inside `callr` are not preserved when forwarded to the main process.

Example:

```r
out <- callr::r(
  \() {
     cli::ansi_palette_show()
  },
  show = TRUE
)
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f2265d9-68cd-42f4-bdb7-6133be7ad58d)

## Causes

1. [`cli` uses `message()`, which goes to standard error](https://github.com/r-lib/cli/issues/467#issuecomment-1133937579).
2. The `callr` child process does not necessarily choose the same number of ANSI colors as the parent process.

Evidence of (2):

```r
cli::num_ansi_colors()
#> [1] 256
callr::r(\() cli::num_ansi_colors())
#> [1] 1
```

## Manual workarounds

1. Redirect stderr to stdout.
2. Inside the `callr` child process, set the `cli.num_colors` option to the correct number of colors.

Example:

```r
out <- callr::r(
  \() {
     options(cli.num_colors = 256)
     cli::ansi_palette_show()
  },
  show = TRUE,
  stderr = "2>&1"
)
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e771da15-b578-47fe-94e3-0926538472f3)

## Request

Is there a way to make `cli` colors "just work" (TM) using the defaults of both packages? I'm not sure what would need to change, but I do believe that aligning the child process colors with those of the parent would be the most intuitive and convenient default behavior.

title: r_process subclass shouldn't be cloneable

``` r
callr::r_bg(\() {})
```

title: r_bg processes hang when waiting for others to spawn
description:
Hi, 

I'm using r_bg in a custom function to manage my parallel processing needs. As part of this, I have written a `for` loop that automatically spawns a set number of background tasks that process small chunks of a larger dataset depending on how many CPU cores I want to use. 

The code itself is quite simple: 

```
for (..i in 1:.num_workers) {
assign(
        x = paste("chunk_", ..i, sep = ""), 
        value = callr::r_bg(
          cmdargs = c(.temp_path, ..i),
          args = list("f" = function_current_instance),
          func = function_to_run
        )
      )
```

However, I am noticing a huge issue, especially with large datasets, that the individual child R processes take a long time to spawn - which is understandable but what happens is that once the child processes are all loaded up, **they hang until the `for` loop in the parent process is finished.**

I have attached a screenshot of this issue - the R process at the very bottom has freshly spawned, and takes around 20 seconds to fully load in. The bunch of R processes at the top have already finished loading and are ready to go, but are somehow paused. 

It seems like there's some dependency on waiting for the parent R process to be free, and the pausing even happens mid-execution if one worker finishes and a new one is spawning. **Is there any way to prevent this pausing of child processes?**

I am on R 4.3.0, ubuntu 20.04 LTS, kernel 5.15.0-89

Many thanks in advance

title: clear tempdir directories when finished?
description:
This is really a `processx` issue, but easier to describe here: `callr::r_bg()` creates one or more new `/tmp/Rtmp*` directories (on *nix, other equivalents on other ODs) each time it is called, and these are left semi-permanently. It should be fairly easy to remove them one the `processx` process is exited. Would that be possible, please?

Motivation: It is not uncommon to need to examine the contents of `tempdir()` outside R, yet this becomes very difficult when there are hundreds of `/tmp/Rtmp*` directories created by exited `processx` instances that have not cleaned these up.

title: To what extent is `callr::r_safe` safe?
description:
From experience, code evaluated with `callr::r_safe` can read environment variables from `/proc/*/environ`, and modify the files `${TMPDIR}/<random>/callr-client--<version>.so` and `${TMPDIR}/<random>/callr-env-<random>` which enables hijacking other evaluation sessions. The serialized input and output files of other sessions can also be read provided `callr::r_safe` is run in parallel (or that those files are not properly cleaned up).

What does `safe` mean in `callr::r_safe`?

title: rsession `get_running_time()` method
description:
Hi Gábor!

I think there is a problem with the `get_running_time()` method for rsession objects. Whenever one of the two uptime values (either the total or current) exists, `rs_get_running_time` calculates a difftime, but when the session has finished the total uptime is specified by `as.POSIXct(NA)` leading to this error:

``` r
rs <- callr::r_session$new()
rs$get_running_time()
#> Error in as.POSIXct.default(e): do not know how to convert 'e' to class "POSIXct"
```

<sup>Created on 2022-12-17 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

I'm running the current dev build 0a099b20ef27d9810cefcdf6a5c52c34e9b59d3c 

Relevant code snippet:

https://github.com/r-lib/callr/blob/0a099b20ef27d9810cefcdf6a5c52c34e9b59d3c/R/r-session.R#L539-L544

If -- and this is **always** a big if 😁 -- I've understood the intended role of this method, I think it's an easy fix. The edits in https://github.com/djnavarro/callr/tree/hotfix-get-running-time modify `rs_get_running_time` to alwasy return a pair of difftimes, never POSIXct objects. The first value is NA if the session is finished, the second value is NA if the session is finished or idle:

```r
rs_get_running_time <- function(self, private) {
  now <- Sys.time()
  finished <- private$state == "finished"
  idle <- private$state == "idle"
  no_uptime <- as.difftime(NA_real_, units = "secs")
  c(total = if (finished) no_uptime else now - private$started_at,
    current = if (finished | idle) no_uptime else now - private$fun_started_at)
}
```

I haven't written any tests but I did check that it seems to do something sensible: returns `c(NA, NA)` for a finished session, uptime for the current call reverts to `NA` as soon as `session$read()` is called, and uptime for any subsequent calls is indeed measured from its own start time not the time at which any preceding calls were started.

Happy to add a couple of tests and send a PR if that's at all helpful 😄

title: Could callr support user hooks?
description:
My specific use-case is klmr/box#199. The package ‘box’ needs to figure out which script file it is called from. It uses the script filename on the R command line for this, and since ‘callr’ creates a temporary script path, ‘box’ goes looking for modules in that temporary path, rather than in the (user’s) calling code’s path. `getwd()` does *not* work, since the working directory is generally unrelated to the script path. Likewise `here::here()` won’t work (in fact, it falls back to `getwd()` in the situations I care about).

The linked issue shows a workaround, but that requires users to add code to both the caller and the callee. Ideally I’d like to add automatic support for ‘callr’ to ‘box’ but I believe this requires support *from* ‘callr’.

As far as I can tell ‘callr’ currently has no way of finding the calling script’s path: I can’t find any indication in its environment variables, the command line or the options. In fact, finding the calling script’s path in R is nontrivial (the ‘box’ implementation is [~100 SLOC](https://github.com/klmr/box/blob/76e8e4f4f205c65d9a748eb2f31329919d20f18b/R/loaded.r#L111-L190), and hard-codes special handling for RStudio and for several packages).


I’ll admit that there’s limited usefulness for this outside of this specific case. And to have a solution that doesn’t depend on ‘box’ my suggestion would be to add a user hook for `callr:::run_r` which can modify the command line options being passed to the R subprocess (or the environment variables).

If I submitted such a PR, would it be considered for inclusion?

title: callr::rscript -> Will continue to execute script even after error, when options()$error is not NULL
description:
When I define options(error = ...) inside an R script, callr::rscript will continue to execute the script even in case of errors.

Reproducible example:
```R
script_content <- "
message('The function that will be executed on error (empty):')
print(options()$error)
options(error = function(){cat('Do something on error.\n')})

message('Some output.')
cat('Other output.\n')
stop('error')
message('This should not be seen in console output.')"

writeLines(script_content,  "call-script.R")

callr::rscript("call-script.R")
```

The output is (the ordering is not always the same):
```R
The function that will be executed on error (empty):
NULL
Some output.
Other output.
Error: error
This should not be seen in console output.
Do something on error.
```

Notice "__This should not be seen in console output.__".

This does not happen when callr:r is used:
```R
callr::r((function(){
  options(error = function(){cat('Do something on error.\n')})
  stop("error")
  message("This should not happen.")
}))
```
Output:
```R
Error: callr subprocess failed: error
Type .Last.error.trace to see where the error occurred
Do something on error.
```

title: Q: Does r_bg() return a failed process if R fails to start?
description:
Hi. Assume that `./.Rprofile` produces an error during the R startup process, then `callr::r()` fails, e.g.

```r
library(callr)

## Run this example in the temporary folder
opwd <- setwd(tempdir())

## An .Rprofile that produces an error
cat("stop('boom')", file=".Rprofile")

v <- r(function() 42)
#> Error in get_result(output = out, options) : 
#>  callr subprocess failed: could not start R, exited with
#>  non-zero status, has crashed or was killed
```

Similarly with `r_bg()`:

```r
p <- r_bg(function() 42)
p$get_result()
#> Error in get_result(output = out, options) : 
#>  callr subprocess failed: could not start R, exited with
#>  non-zero status, has crashed or was killed
```

Now, when I inspect `p` (an `r_process` object), I can see that it failed:

```sh
p$is_alive()
#> [1] FALSE

p$get_exit_status()
#> [1] 1
```

My question is, does it fail already before `r_bg()` returns, or can it happen later?  I'm trying to decide if:

```r
p <- r_bg(function() 42)
if (p$get_exit_status() != 0) stop("Failed to launch R process")
```

is sufficient, or it could be that it fails afterwards and I have to wait for a while, e.g.

```r
p <- r_bg(function() 42)
Sys.sleep(10) ## wait long enough
if (p$get_exit_status() != 0) stop("Failed to launch R process")
```

title: Support to specify 32-bit R
description: With [RStudio's plans to drop support for 32-bit R](https://community.rstudio.com/t/unable-to-select-32-bit-r-version-in-rstudio-v1-2-1047-1-preview/16404/9?u=jpshanno), there are going to be a number of users who can't connect to existing datasets. To get around this problem I wrote a few functions to fetch sql queries with 32-bit Rscript and pass the data back to my active RStudio session. It would be nice if people in my situation, and the people in the thread above, could leverage callr to access their data. It wouldn't be a complete fix to the problem, since it would require a new connection to the data source each time callr is used, but I think it would help out in a lot of use cases. I'd be happy to contribute if this is something that moves forward.

description:
`callr::r` seems to interfere with the `install.packages` `lib` parameter (R version 3.6.0).
`package1` is already installed in `/tmp/lib`. `package2` imports package1:

```r
callr::r(function() {
  install.packages("/tmp/dev/package2", lib = "/tmp/lib", repos = NULL, type = "source") 
})
```

prints

> Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘package2’ in loadNamespace(i, c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[i]]):
>  there is no package called ‘package1’

Looks like the main problem is overwriting the `.libPaths` in the files defined in `R_PROFILE ` and `R_PROFILE_USER ` interpreted by `R CMD install`:

```r
.libPaths(c("/usr/local/lib/R/site-library", "/usr/local/lib/R/library"))
```

When unsetting corresponding environment variables (or manually removing the `.libPaths` calls), this seems to work again:

```r
callr::r(function() {
  Sys.unsetenv(c("R_ENVIRON", "R_ENVIRON_USER", "R_PROFILE", "R_PROFILE_USER"))
  install.packages("/tmp/dev/package2", lib = "/tmp/lib", repos = NULL, type = "source") 
})
```

This is not an issue with R version 3.5.1.

title: Error message sent to stdout instead of stderr
description:
Hi @gaborcsardi. Thanks for an awesome package. It is a critical piece of infrastructure for my package [workflowr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=workflowr). Recently my CI builds started failing, and I realized this was due to callr 3.0.0 that was released to CRAN a few weeks ago. My unit tests expect the error message to be sent to stderr (as done by callr 2.0.4), but now the error message is written to stdout (for both 3.0.0 and 3.0.0.9000). Would it be possible to return to the previous behavior, or is the plan going forward to write errors to the stdout stream? If the new behavior is desired, would it be possible to document this more prominently? I read the [NEWS for processx 3.2.0](https://github.com/r-lib/processx/blob/5917b062f4033c3c6cd71fb6b76d012611e04614/inst/NEWS.md#processx-320), the [NEWS for callr 3.0.0](https://github.com/r-lib/callr/blob/10c1269ae0daf42f0d18f5a198546947f6a6c930/NEWS.md#callr-300), the [callr section on Standard output and error](https://github.com/r-lib/callr/tree/10c1269ae0daf42f0d18f5a198546947f6a6c930#standard-output-and-error), and the man page for `callr::r`. I couldn't find anything about redirecting error messages to stdout. Below I document the previous behavior as well as the latest behavior. For all examples, I used the following function: ``` f <- function() { print("send to stdout") message("send to stderr") stop("send to stderr") } ``` callr 2.0.4 sends the error message to stderr (though it includes additional error messages). ``` devtools::install_version("callr", version = "2.0.4") library("callr") callr::r(f, stdout = "stdout.txt", stderr = "stderr.txt") # Error in (function () : send to stderr cat(readLines("stdout.txt"), sep = "\n") # [1] "send to stdout" cat(readLines("stderr.txt"), sep = "\n") # send to stderr # Error in (function () : send to stderr # Calls: withCallingHandlers -> saveRDS -> do.call -> -> # Execution halted ``` The current CRAN version (3.0.0) sends the error message to stdout. ``` install.packages("callr") packageVersion("callr") # [1] ‘3.0.0’ library("callr") callr::r(f, stdout = "stdout.txt", stderr = "stderr.txt") # Error in (function () : send to stderr cat(readLines("stdout.txt"), sep = "\n") # [1] "send to stdout" # cat(readLines("stderr.txt"), sep = "\n") # send to stderr ``` The current version on GitHub (3.0.0.9000) sends the error message to stdout. ``` devtools::install_github("r-lib/callr") packageVersion("callr") # [1] ‘3.0.0.9000’ library("callr") callr::r(f, stdout = "stdout.txt", stderr = "stderr.txt") # Error in (function () : send to stderr cat(readLines("stdout.txt"), sep = "\n") # [1] "send to stdout" # cat(readLines("stderr.txt"), sep = "\n") # send to stderr ```

title: Rethink setting the lib path in the child process
description:
The goal is to make sure that these are always the same:
```r
.libPaths()
callr::r(function()  .libPaths())
callr::r(function() callr::r(function()  .libPaths()))
```
and the same for `.Library` and  also  `.Library.site`.

The lib path can be set in various places:
* inherited `R_LIBS` + `R_LIBS_USER` +  `R_LIBS_SITE` env vars
* system .Renviron (`R_ENVIRON or `R_HOME/etc/Renviron.site`)
* user .Renviron (`R_ENVIRON_USER` or `./.Renviron` or `~.Renviron`)
* system .Rprofile (`R_PROFILE` or  `R_HOME/etc/Rprofile.site`)
* user .Rprofile (`R_PROFILE_USER` or  `./.Rprofile` or `~/.Rprofile`)
* R session via `.libPaths()`

Our strategy is to make sure that `.Library`, `.Library.site` and  `.libPaths()` are all the same in the child process, and that they are set up in such a way that the whole child tree inherits their value.  (Unless a process changes them deliberately.)

## .Library

This is always the system library and we can't modify it. So we don't need to do anything with this.

## .Library.site

This can come from
1.  inherited env var  `R_LIBS_SITE`
2. system `.Renviron` `R_LIBS_SITE`
3. user `.Renviron` `R_LIBS_SITE`
4. system `Rprofile.site` setting directly

So we set this in the system profile. We set `R_PROFILE` to point to this file.
* if the profile was requested, we make a copy of it,  and add setting `.Library.site`.
* if the profile was not requested, we just include setting `.Library.site`.

R sessions with `--no-site-file`, will get the proper `.Library.site` if it was set via `R_LIBS_SITE` somewhere. Otherwise they won't, which makes sense.

## .libPaths()

This is similar, but can also be set in the user profile, and in the session itself as well. So we create a fake user session file as well, and set it there as well, and the fake system session file as well.

```R
r_env_vars <- function() {
  vars <- c(
    "R_LIBS" = paste(.libPaths(), collapse = .Platform$path.sep),
    "CYGWIN" = "nodosfilewarning",
    # When R CMD check runs tests, it sets R_TESTS. When the tests
    # themselves run R CMD xxxx, as is the case with the tests in
    # devtools, having R_TESTS set causes errors because it confuses
    # the R subprocesses. Un-setting it here avoids those problems.
    "R_TESTS" = "",
    "R_BROWSER" = "false",
    "R_PDFVIEWER" = "false",
    "TAR" = auto_tar())

  if (is.na(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN", unset = NA))) {
    vars[["NOT_CRAN"]] <- "true"
  }

  vars
}

# Determine the best setting for the TAR environmental variable
# This is needed for R <= 2.15.2 to use internal tar. Later versions don't need
# this workaround, and they use R_BUILD_TAR instead of TAR, so this has no
# effect on them.
auto_tar <- function() {
  tar <- Sys.getenv("TAR", unset = NA)
  if (!is.na(tar)) return(tar)

  windows <- .Platform$OS.type == "windows"
  no_rtools <- is.null(get_rtools_path())
  if (windows && no_rtools) "internal" else ""
}
```
